name: moon
note: Tidally locked, so it always shows Earth the same face. Drifting away from us about 3.8 cm a year.

name: phobos
note: Orbits faster than Mars rotates, so it rises in the west and sets in the east twice a day. Spiralling inward and will break up in roughly 50 million years.

name: deimos
note: Only about 12 km across. From the Martian surface it looks like a bright star, not a disc.

name: io
note: The most volcanically active body in the solar system. Tidal flexing from Jupiter keeps its interior molten.

name: europa
note: A saltwater ocean under an ice shell, holding perhaps twice the water of all Earth's oceans combined.

name: ganymede
note: The largest moon in the solar system, bigger than Mercury, and the only one with its own magnetic field.

name: callisto
note: The most heavily cratered object known. Its surface has barely changed in four billion years.

name: titan
note: The only moon with a thick atmosphere, and the only other world with liquid on its surface: rivers and seas of methane.

name: enceladus
note: Fires water plumes from its south pole through cracks in the ice. Those plumes feed Saturn's E ring.

name: triton
note: Orbits backwards, which means Neptune captured it rather than forming with it. Almost certainly a Kuiper Belt object.
